common.nothingToShow: Nothing to show in the {{view}} view.
hint.lowConfidence: The recommender has little data for some containers yet: the recommendation may still change a lot.
hint.fetchingHistory: The recommender is still loading history: the recommendation may still change.
hint.configUnsupported: The recommender cannot use this VPA: its target cannot be read, or it is not the topmost controller (point the VPA at the Deployment, not at its ReplicaSet). It gives no recommendation.
hint.noPodsMatched: No running pod belongs to the target: it has no replicas, or its pods do not run. The recommender needs pods to measure.
hint.noPodsNow: No pod matches this VPA right now (the target is scaled to zero or between runs). The recommender keeps its last recommendation, and the next pods get it.
hint.notProvided: The recommender has not produced a recommendation yet.
hint.noStatus: No status yet: the recommender has not looked at this VPA, or no recommender runs for it.
hint.deprecated: The recommender says this configuration is deprecated and will stop being supported.
modeExplain.Off: Recommends only: the VPA never changes pods.
modeExplain.Initial: Sets the resources when a pod is created; running pods are never changed.
modeExplain.Recreate: Sets the resources when a pod is created, and the updater evicts a running pod whose requests are outside the recommended range (or, after 12 hours, differ by 10% or more), so it is created again with the recommendation. By default it evicts nothing while fewer than 2 replicas run.
modeExplain.Auto: A deprecated name of Recreate, and works the same way: the resources are set when a pod is created, and the updater evicts running pods whose requests are far from the recommendation.
modeExplain.InPlaceOrRecreate: Sets the resources when a pod is created, and the updater resizes running pods in place, evicting them only where an in-place resize is not possible. Needs the cluster's InPlacePodVerticalScaling feature.
modeExplain.InPlace: Sets the resources when a pod is created, and the updater only resizes running pods in place, never evicting them. Needs the VPA components' InPlace feature gate and the cluster's InPlacePodVerticalScaling feature.
modeExplain.unknown: The mode {{mode}} is not one this version of Sextant knows.
target.notServed: The cluster does not serve the target's kind {{kind}}.
target.notRead: The target has not been read: it does not exist, or it cannot be read.
recommendation.title: Recommendation and the next pods
table.containerOff: Not scaled: the container's policy is Off
table.noContainers: The target's pod template has no containers.
table.notInTemplate: Also recommended for containers that are not in the template (added when the pod is created, such as sidecars): {{containers}}.
table.how: A pod created now gets the target as its request; its limit keeps the template's ratio of limit to request, as the admission controller computes it, and a missing limit stays missing.
table.howRequestsOnly: With RequestsOnly the request is never set above the container's limit, and the limit stays as it is; with RequestsAndLimits the limit keeps the template's ratio of limit to request.
table.notModelled: Not taken into account here: a LimitRange of the namespace, containers that other webhooks add, and the startup CPU boost.
conflict.line: HPA {{hpa}} scales this workload on {{resources}}, which this VPA changes in mode {{mode}}: the two fight.
conflict.why: When the VPA raises a request, the HPA's utilization falls and it removes replicas; the remaining pods use more, and so on. Scale the HPA on another metric, leave the VPA in Off or Initial, or let the VPA control only the other resource.
conflict.valueLine: HPA {{hpa}} scales this workload on the average {{resources}} per pod (AverageValue), which this VPA changes in mode {{mode}}. A new request does not move that average, so the two do not fight directly, but both react to the same usage: watch that they do not keep undoing each other.
components.title: VPA components
components.missing.recommender: Recommendations come from the recommender: without it this VPA gets none.
components.missing.admission: Without the admission controller pods are created with the template's values: the recommendation reaches no new pod, and evicted pods come back unchanged.
components.missing.admissionInitial: Without the admission controller, Initial does nothing: pods are created with the template's values.
components.missing.updater: Without the updater running pods are never changed: only pods created for other reasons get the recommendation.
components.managed: Looked for as the Deployments vpa-recommender, vpa-updater and vpa-admission-controller in kube-system, and by the labels of the VPA Helm charts. Where VPA is a managed add-on (as on GKE), its components run outside the cluster.
workload.title: Vertical Pod Autoscaler
workload.several_one: {{count}} VPA targets this workload: for its pods only the oldest one counts.
workload.several_other: {{count}} VPAs target this workload: for its pods only the oldest one counts.
